Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J
1. Mr. V.B.S. Negi, learned Senior
Counsel with Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Vikas
Pande and Mr. Yogesh Kum ar Pacholia,
learned counsel for the petitioners.
2. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. Neeraj Garg, learned counsel for
the respondent-UPNL.
4. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel
for the respondent-University.
5. Since com m on questions of fact and
law are involved in these petitions,
therefore, these petitions are clubbed
together and decided by this com m on
judgm ent. However, for the sake of brevity
and convenience, facts of WPSS No. 579 of
2024 alone are being considered and
discussed.
6. Writ Petition (S/ S) No. 579 of 2024 is
filed by 44 persons, who were engaged on
contract through UPNL for perform ing duties
of Group 'C' and Group 'D' em ployees.
According to petitioners, they were engaged
in Uttarakhand Ayurved University between
2013 to 2021 and they continuously served
as such, to the satisfaction of all concerned,
till January, 2024.
7. According to petitioners, in January,
2024, they were disengaged form service
without any rhym e and reason. Feeling
aggrieved by their disengagem ent,
petitioners filed this writ petition seeking the
following reliefs: -

2025:UHC:8618
(i) issue writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent no. 1, 2
and 3 to permit the petitioners to continue their
engagement against their respective post in the
University and pay them salary/ remuneration
on monthly basis.
(ii) issue writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent no. 2 and 3
to pay the arrears of the salary/ remuneration to
the petitioners which has not been paid from
the month of November, 2023 to till date.
(iii) issue writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent no. 1, 2 &
3 not to interfere in the peaceful functioning of
the petitioners or not to change and alter the
status of the petitioners.
8. Learned counsels for the petitioners
have relied upon an order dated 25.04.2024
passed by Division Bench of this Court in
SPA No. 116 of 2024. Operative portion of
the said order is extracted below: -
"7. On the next date of hearing, learned counsel for
respondent nos. 2 and 3 will clarify as to when
the advertisement for filling up the posts by
way of regular selection is going to be m ade,
and till then, the appellants will continue to
work.
8. Counter-affidavit be filed within four weeks.
9. List this matter on 24.07.2024.
10. Respondents will not make any appointment
through outsourcing before starting the regular
selection and along with the counter-affidavit,
advertisement will be placed on record."
9. Mr. V.B.S. Negi, learned Senior
Counsel appearing for the petitioners points
out that pursuant to order dated 25.04.2024
passed by Division Bench, 42 contract
em ployees, engaged through outsourcing,
were re-engaged, vide order dated
11.09.2024 and they are continuously
serving thereafter.
10. Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, learned counsel
appearing for petitioners in WPSS No. 2448
of 2024 subm its that on 11.09.2024 itself,
another order was issued by Registrar of the
University, whereby 93 contract em ployees
were disengaged, including som e petitioners

2025:UHC:8618
in these writ petitions.
11. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel
for the University subm its that selection
process was initiated for supplying available
vacancies on Group 'C' and Group 'D' posts
in the University by issuing an
advertisem ent, however, it was later found
that there are no Rules governing m ode of
recruitm ent for certain posts and various
other anom alies were also found, therefore,
University requested the State Governm ent
to cancel the selection process. He, thus,
concedes that as of now, there is no
selection ongoing in respect of the available
vacancies.
12. Learned counsel for University further
subm its that State Governm ent, vide
Governm ent Order dated 25.04.2025 has
restrained the University from engaging any
Group 'C' and Group 'D' em ployee on
contract or through outsourcing against any
sanctioned vacant post. He subm its that
pursuant to orders passed by this Court in
Writ Petitions as well as in Special Appeal,
University requested the State Governm ent
to grant perm ission to com ply the order
passed by this Court by re-engaging the
contract em ployees, however, he concedes
that after Governm ent Order dated
25.04.2025, no further com m unication was
issued by the University.
13. From the subm issions m ade by learned
counsel for the University, this Court can
gather that University is also facing difficulty
in m anaging its affairs due to large num ber
of vacancies on Group 'C' and Group 'D'
posts. Som e of the petitioners have been
serving on contract for last m ore than ten
years; their work and conduct has been
found to be satisfactory, therefore,
disengaging such contract em ployees, who
rendered satisfactory service for long period
of tim e, without any reason or justification,
does not appear to be proper. Moreover, no

2025:UHC:8618
University can be run without sufficient
num ber of teaching and non-teaching staff.
14. I n such view of the m atter, the writ
petitions are disposed of with a direction to
Secretary, Departm ent of AYUSH to re-visit
the Policy contained in Governm ent Order
dated 25.04.2025 and consider granting
perm ission to the University to engage
contract em ployees, till the available
vacancies are filled by regularly em ployees
selected persons.
15. This Court hopes and expects that
Secretary concerned shall take decision in
the m atter within six weeks from the date of
presentation of certified copy of this order.
16. Such of the petitioners, who have not
been paid rem uneration, even though they
rendered service as contract em ployee, shall
be at liberty to m ake representation for
release of outstanding dues. The
representation, if m ade by such em ployees,
shall be decided by Registrar of the
University, within four weeks from the date
of receipt of certified copy of this order.
17. For a period of eight weeks or till
petitioners are re-engaged, whichever is
earlier, such of the petitioners, who have
been provided official accom m odation, shall
not be asked to vacate the sam e.
